title: Azure VM unreachable over SSH or RDP
symptoms: A connection times out or is refused although the VM appears provisioned.
The issue started after an address, image, or network change.

diagnostic_steps.step: Check service health and VM state
diagnostic_steps.check: Portal: VM Overview, Resource Health, Boot diagnostics; CLI: `az vm get-instance-view -g <rg> -n <vm>`.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Confirm power state, provisioning state, boot status, and whether the guest reached its login screen.

diagnostic_steps.check: Network Watcher: IP flow verify and effective security rules; review NIC/subnet NSGs and effective routes.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Identify a deny rule, wrong next hop, missing route, or expected port 22/3389 blocked.

diagnostic_steps.check: Review guest firewall/service status through approved serial console or recovery path; verify client egress and current VM IP.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Determine whether traffic reaches the guest and whether SSH/RDP listens on the expected interface and port.

root_cause_reasoning: A timeout points toward a path or firewall issue; an immediate refusal often indicates the host is reachable but the service is not listening. Boot diagnostics and flow evidence help distinguish them.
safe_remediation: Correct the narrowest confirmed NSG, route, guest firewall, or service configuration issue.
Use Bastion or approved private access where possible; restrict any temporary inbound rule to a trusted source and remove it after validation.
safety_notes: Do not open SSH/RDP to the whole internet as a diagnostic shortcut.
Snapshot or confirm recoverability before guest-level repair; avoid restarting a healthy production workload without impact review.

title: Network security group blocks application traffic
symptoms: Requests to a VM or service time out from one subnet or client range.
A recent NSG or subnet change is suspected.

diagnostic_steps.check: Collect client IP, destination private/public IP, protocol, port, direction, and timestamp.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: You can compare a specific flow against security rules rather than broad guesses.

diagnostic_steps.check: Network Watcher: IP flow verify for the target NIC and five-tuple.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: The result identifies the matching allow or deny rule and its associated NSG.

diagnostic_steps.check: Inspect NIC and subnet NSG associations, rule priorities, effective routes, and peering/firewall path.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Find priority conflicts, wrong source range, or a route sending traffic through an unexpected appliance.

root_cause_reasoning: NSGs are stateful and independently associated at subnet and NIC scopes; an allow in one place does not override a matching deny at another effective scope.
safe_remediation: Correct the specific rule or association with least privilege and documented ownership.
Validate the exact flow from the intended source, then monitor denied flows and remove obsolete temporary rules.
safety_notes: Do not add an any-to-any allow rule.
Do not assume a rule visible on the NIC is the only effective policy.

title: Web application returns HTTP 5xx errors
symptoms: Users report intermittent or sustained HTTP 5xx responses.
The pattern may correlate with a deployment or dependency slowdown.

diagnostic_steps.check: Application Insights: failed requests, availability, dependency duration; compare with deployment timeline.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Establish affected routes, instances, status codes, and whether failures began after a release.

diagnostic_steps.check: App Service Diagnose and solve problems, HTTP logs, application logs, platform metrics, health checks.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Look for worker restarts, resource exhaustion, startup failures, and platform-generated 502/503/504 responses.

diagnostic_steps.check: Review database/API dependency failures, DNS, certificates, connection strings, and slot-specific settings.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Identify an upstream timeout, invalid setting, authentication failure, or resource saturation.

root_cause_reasoning: A 5xx label alone does not identify the failing layer. Correlated traces, platform logs, and exact status code distinguish application exceptions from gateway or worker failures.
safe_remediation: If impact is broad and a prior version is healthy, use the established rollback or slot swap process after checking data compatibility.
Fix the demonstrated dependency, configuration, or capacity issue; validate with synthetic checks and telemetry.
safety_notes: Avoid restarting or scaling before capturing diagnostic evidence.
Do not expose secrets or personal data in logs while increasing diagnostic verbosity.

title: Managed identity cannot access a resource
symptoms: Workload obtains a token but a target operation returns 403.
A role assignment or resource move may have recently occurred.

diagnostic_steps.check: Check workload identity configuration and resource logs; confirm principal/object ID and token audience.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: The caller is the expected system- or user-assigned identity and the token targets the intended service.

diagnostic_steps.check: Review Azure RBAC assignments and required data-plane role at the resource, group, or subscription scope.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: A missing role, wrong principal, inherited-scope mismatch, or control-plane-only role is visible.

diagnostic_steps.check: Review target firewall/private endpoint/DNS settings and audit/diagnostic logs; allow for role propagation.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Distinguish authorization denial from network rejection and validate the resolved endpoint.

root_cause_reasoning: Successful token acquisition proves authentication but not authorization. Storage and Key Vault data operations commonly require a data-plane role distinct from resource management permissions.
safe_remediation: Assign the minimum supported role to the correct principal at the narrowest scope, then retest with a fresh token after propagation.
Correct DNS or network policy only when diagnostics show that layer is responsible.
safety_notes: Do not grant Owner or broad Contributor just to make the error disappear.
Do not log bearer tokens or secret values.

title: Storage access fails due to permissions or networking
symptoms: A client receives authorization failure or cannot resolve/reach the storage endpoint.
Access works from one network but not another.

diagnostic_steps.check: Capture error code, caller identity, operation, endpoint hostname, source network, and timestamp.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Authorization failures differ from DNS, firewall, and transport errors.

diagnostic_steps.check: Inspect token principal and Storage Blob Data role assignment at the right scope.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: The identity has a data-plane role that permits the requested operation.

diagnostic_steps.check: Review firewall virtual network/IP rules, private endpoint state, DNS zone links, and resolved address.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: The client resolves to the intended endpoint and its source network is allowed.

root_cause_reasoning: Storage authorization and network controls are independent gates. A valid identity cannot bypass a firewall, and management-plane access does not automatically grant data access.
safe_remediation: Grant only the required data role and allow the intended source network or private endpoint path.
Retest read/write behavior from the target network and review storage diagnostic logs.
safety_notes: Avoid account keys or broad SAS as a permanent workaround.
Do not disable the firewall to test production access.

title: Application has high latency or resource consumption
symptoms: p95 response time increases and users see slow requests.
CPU, memory, dependency duration, or queue depth may be elevated.

diagnostic_steps.check: Application Insights: request duration, operation traces, failures, dependency calls, and deployment markers.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Determine which route, instance, and dependency dominates latency.

diagnostic_steps.check: Azure Monitor: CPU, memory where available, network, throttling, queue depth, and autoscale events.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Find sustained saturation or a scale rule that reacts too late or reaches a cap.

diagnostic_steps.check: Use bounded KQL queries and compare instances, regions, recent releases, and dependency behavior.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Isolate application, database, network, or downstream-service contribution.

root_cause_reasoning: End-to-end latency is additive across request processing and dependencies. Scaling the front end may not help when the database, downstream API, or lock contention is the bottleneck.
safe_remediation: Mitigate the measured bottleneck with a tested change, capacity adjustment, query fix, or dependency protection.
Confirm latency and error-rate recovery and update alert thresholds/runbooks based on evidence.
safety_notes: Do not dump sensitive payloads into logs.
Avoid scaling blindly; it can increase cost or overload downstream dependencies.

title: Service needs backup or recovery
symptoms: A workload owner requests recovery after deletion, corruption, or regional outage.
Recovery requirements are unclear or untested.

diagnostic_steps.check: Record affected data, acceptable data loss (RPO), restoration time (RTO), region, and dependencies.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: You have approved targets and know whether point-in-time restore or disaster failover is needed.

diagnostic_steps.check: Check Azure Backup jobs, policy, vault, retention, soft delete/protection settings, and latest usable recovery point.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Confirm the correct workload is protected and determine recovery-point age and health.

diagnostic_steps.check: Review supported restore/failover workflow, target network, identity, DNS, capacity, and owner validation.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: A nonproduction test path exists and will not overwrite production data or disrupt replication.

root_cause_reasoning: Backup restores data to a point in time; disaster recovery replicates and orchestrates service continuity. Select based on the failure and RPO/RTO rather than treating them as interchangeable.
safe_remediation: Use an approved restore or test failover to an isolated target, validate data and application integrity, and record measured recovery time.
Coordinate DNS/routing changes and production cutover only through the incident or change owner.
safety_notes: Do not overwrite a live system before validating the restore point.
Do not assume a green backup job proves application-consistent recovery.

title: Unexpected Azure bill requires investigation
symptoms: A team notices a material increase in estimated or invoiced spend.
The source resource or meter is not obvious.

diagnostic_steps.step: Set billing scope and compare periods
diagnostic_steps.check: Cost Management: select correct billing scope, date range, granularity, and compare with prior period.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: The increase is isolated to subscription, service, resource, or meter and actual versus forecast is understood.

diagnostic_steps.check: Group by resource, service, meter, region, and tag; review Activity Log and deployment history.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Find newly created resources, usage growth, changed tier, backup/log ingestion, or data transfer.

diagnostic_steps.check: Review reservations/savings-plan utilization, marketplace, networking, monitoring, and storage retention.
diagnostic_steps.expected_observation: Separate covered compute from independent charges and identify ongoing resources.

root_cause_reasoning: A total bill rarely identifies the cause. Break down usage and correlate timestamps with deployment and consumption data; billing data can have reporting delay.
safe_remediation: Confirm the owning team and business impact before stopping or downsizing resources.
Apply approved schedules, retention, rightsizing, or removal after dependency checks; configure budget alerts and tag standards.
safety_notes: A budget alert is not a spending cap.
Do not delete a resource solely because its cost is unfamiliar; verify owner, dependencies, and recovery requirements first.
